AC2 (GATE-A/B pass — novel HIGH, no recurrence): fresh row, effective_severity >= HIGH, no open board row, recurrence_count < 2 → Opus DOES spawn (regression guard).

AC3 (GATE-B Tier 1 blocks — concrete MBB regression fixture): same (ticker,quarter,trigger_id) recurs while REFLOW-<ticker>-<quarter> (or any non-terminal row referencing guard_key) is open → NO Opus spawn; both locks released; row terminal. AC4 (GATE-B Tier 2 blocks — bootstrap net): no board row yet, but signals_processed holds >=2 rows with identical (type,ticker,quarter,trigger_id,context) → NO Opus spawn; reflow-needed-hint emitted to po; row terminal.
AC5 (GATE-B Tier 2 passes on count==1): no board row, first-ever occurrence → Opus spawns (never suppress genuine first finding).
AC6 (self-healing): board row transitions to TERMINAL_SET status → Tier 1 stops blocking even though recurrence_count remains >=2 (regression test for stuck-forever risk).

mandates: GATE-A: effective_severity = row.severity (top-level field, authoritative) with static ESC-id tier fallback (ONLY when row.severity missing); floor=HIGH from SignalSeverityEnum (orchStateSchema.ts:172); NOT max-of-both (would re-escalate shipped ESC-4 AC-2 INFO downgrade).

GATE-B Tier 1: read-only jq board-row-exists check on REFLOW-<ticker>-<quarter> (PO's live convention) with NON-terminal status per TERMINAL_SET (orchStateSchema.ts:58-64); self-healing on status flip to terminal.

Terminal Exit: both gates converge here on FAIL; release spawn_key (claimed in Step 2, must be freed immediately if gates decide not to spawn); release guard_key; mark row terminal per Step 6 pattern.

Injection safety: jq --arg/--argjson only, NEVER interpolate signal payload into /bin/sh; drain-signals.js CLI subcommand uses bound-param escaping (escB helper), matching existing sqlEsc() convention.

p1_5.depends_on: P1 (needs owner_client_session to attribute an expired lock to a SPECIFIC dead session so a DIFFERENT same-role session can adopt it — impossible under owner_agent role-key)
p1_5.may_parallel: P2 (detection-by-staleness works pre-P2; detection precision improves once P2 presence roster lets the reaper cross-check an expired lock against the live-session roster)
p1_5.mechanism: Server-side reaper in the always-on mcp-server (the ONLY process alive across all session deaths) scans task_locks for expired locks (heartbeat_age > TTL) attributable to a dead session and emits an idempotent re-dispatch signal carrying a durable-checkpoint pointer; a live session ADOPTS and CONTINUES from the checkpoint (task_board status / handoff doc / period-keyed artifact) via stale-steal under its OWN owner_client_session — NOT a fresh restart; poison-task escalation after N retries stops infinite re-dispatch.
p1_5.design_ceiling_accepted: HONEST LIMIT, NOT A DEFECT: zero live sessions = zero execution. The reaper runs in mcp-server (a tool server, not an agent runtime) so it can only mark/keep state ADOPTABLE and emit the re-dispatch signal; actual takeover happens when the NEXT session comes online and reads that signal. Accepted by PO as an architectural limit.
dod_shape: Reaper detects orphan = lock expired (heartbeat_age > TTL) AND owner_client_session attributable to a non-live session (staleness pre-P2; cross-checked vs presence roster post-P2)
Orphaned work becomes ADOPTABLE: reaper emits an idempotent re-dispatch signal carrying the durable-checkpoint pointer (task_id + task_board status + handoff path + period-key)
A live session ADOPTS and CONTINUES from the durable checkpoint (not restart); adoption claims the expired lock via stale-steal with the adopter's owner_client_session
Idempotent continuation — NO double-publish of a period-keyed artifact (reuse published:<kind>:<period-key> dedup; honor guaranteed-slot double-post lesson)
Poison-task escalation: after N failed adoptions, stop re-dispatch, mark poisoned, route to po/BUG (no infinite loop)
Honest ceiling (zero live sessions = zero execution) documented + accepted; reaper runs in always-on mcp-server
RAW-verify against LIVE coordination.db in the Docker named volume
